version.changelog:
SeaArt Video Generator v1.0.0 — Initial Release

- Enables high-quality AI video generation using the SeaArt platform with Text-to-Video and Image-to-Video support.
- Supports multiple generation models including SeaArt Sono Cast (default), Vidu Q3 Turbo, Kling 3.0, and Wan 2.6.
- Allows choice of aspect ratios for text prompts (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4).
- Provides clear instructions for obtaining and securely storing the required SeaArt authentication token.
- Includes guidance on invoking the video generation process and presenting output video URLs.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: seaart-video
Version: 1.0.0

The seaart-video skill is a legitimate integration for generating AI videos via the SeaArt platform. The Python script (scripts/generate.py) uses the requests library to communicate with official seaart.ai API endpoints and handles authentication via a user-provided SEAART_TOKEN stored in environment variables. No evidence of data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious intent was found in the code or the instructions provided in SKILL.md.

llm.summary: The skill is largely coherent for calling SeaArt APIs, but the runtime instructions encourage posting a secret cookie token into chat and contain contradictory/mismatched guidance, which is a security/privacy concern.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, required env var (SEAART_TOKEN), and the included Python script all align with a SeaArt text/image-to-video integration. The network endpoints used are all on seaart.ai and the single required credential (the site's 'T' cookie) is appropriate for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly instructs users to reply in chat with their raw SEAART_TOKEN so the agent can run `/update-config` to save it. That encourages users to place a secret into chat history (and possibly logs or other stores). The SKILL.md also claims the token 'never leaves your machine in plaintext' while simultaneously describing steps that would surface the token in chat and call a platform config tool — this is inconsistent. Additionally an example references a model name ('Minimax') not present in the script's supported models, causing functional mismatch.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote download/install step; the skill is instruction-only plus a local Python script. That limits install risk. The script does require the 'requests' library (not auto-installed), which the README mentions. No arbitrary external archives or unknown URLs are fetched by the installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only SEAART_TOKEN is requested which is proportionate to the task. However, the instructions for obtaining/storing that token (copying the T cookie and pasting into chat) increase the chance of accidental disclosure. The skill claims it does not log/store the token, but instructs use of `/update-config` which will store the value in agent config — this contradiction should be clarified before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not demand elevated system privileges. It does recommend saving the token via `/update-config`, which is normal for credentials but means the token will be persisted by the platform — confirm who can access that stored config. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but isn't combined with other broad permissions here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims (call seaart.ai APIs), but the runtime instructions encourage insecure handling of your SeaArt auth cookie. Do not paste your T cookie into public chat or any channel you don't fully control. Instead: (1) Prefer setting SEAART_TOKEN directly in a secure platform configuration UI or your local environment rather than replying with it in-chat. (2) Confirm exactly where `/update-config` stores secrets and who/what can read them on your platform; if unsure, avoid using that flow. (3) If you must paste the token, treat it as compromised afterward and rotate/revoke it in your SeaArt account. (4) Note the SKILL.md example references a model name not present in the script; expect occasional runtime errors — test with non-sensitive prompts first. (5) Ensure Python 3 and the requests package are installed locally. If you are uncomfortable with storing the token in agent config or with exposing it in chat logs, do not install or enable this skill.
